item.title: Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance Programming Contest 2025 (AtCoder Beginner Contest 402)
item.description:
Contest Information

  • Duration: 100 minutes
  • Rated Range: 0 - 1999
  • This contest is a compensation for the unrated ABC304.

Why Tokio Marine target AtCoder users

Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance Co.,Ltd. needs AtCoder users.

About 140 years ago, we were born as the first Non-Life insurance company in Japan. We started with marine insurance, which support growth of shipping or trade in Meiji period, followed by auto insurance in motorization, earthquake insurance for large-scale earthquake disasters, and cyber risk insurance for the recent networked society. Non-life insurance has been changing with the progress of times. For 140 years since establishment, we have been providing new insurance services for the changing society by quantifying the risks of accidents and disasters based on mathematical models. However, in the current era of technological innovation and digital transformation, we endeavor to transform ourselves more rapidly than ever. To build a safe and secure society by utilizing complex data acquired from the latest digital technologies, IoT equipment and human activities, we strongly believe that talents with algorithm design and programing become a key to our success. We hope, in the future, participants of this contest will create new businesses or support those challenges by using cutting-edge technologies and complicated data, leading to a safe and secure society.

Point Values

Task Score
A 100
B 200
C 300
D 400
E 450
F 525
G 650

Please note

  • If participants would like to receive information from our company or Tokio Marine Group, we may send event information to your email address.
  • To receive a prize (Amazon gift card), it is required to register an email address and agree to the privacy policy in application for this competition. In case that any email address is not registered or there is no agreement to the privacy policy, the participant will not be eligible for the prize.
  • People who reside outside of Japan and Tokio Marine Group employees are not eligible to receive prizes.
  • If for any reason the prize cannot be delivered, we will contact you at your registered email address. If you do not reply within two weeks, the prize will not be awarded.
  • If an awardee becomes ineligible to receive the prize, the award will be presented to the participant who is one rank below.
  • If there are more than one persons with the same ranking, awardees may be decided by lot.

Contest Rules

This contest is full-feedback (solutions are judged during the contest).
When you solve a problem, you get a score assigned to it. Competitors are ranked first by total scores, then by penalties. The penalties are computed as (the time you spend to get your current score) + (5 minutes) * (the number of incorrect attempts).

item.title: The 2nd Masters Championship-qual-
item.description:
Contest Information

  • This contest is a team competition and is not subject to AHC ratings or AWTF selection.
  • This contest is for teams (two or three people). No single participant is allowed.

About AtCoder Heuristic Contest（AHC）

This is a series of programming contests that will be held regularly on AtCoder. Unlike algorithm contests such as ABC/ARC/AGC, the goal is to create a better solution to a problem for which it is difficult to find the optimal solution. For examples of problems, see past contests of similar format.

Rules

  • The Masters Championship will provide tools (input generators and local testers) for both the preliminary and final rounds, but will not provide visualizers.
  • There is one problem, but it is divided into several tasks based on different input generation methods, etc. Rankings will be determined by the sum of the highest scores received for each task during the contest. You can use any programming language available on AtCoder.
  • There is no penalty for resubmission, but you must wait at least 5 minutes between submissions. The 5-minute submission interval limits are per team member, per task, and it is possible to submit to multiple tasks simultaneously.
  • Teams are required to participate in this contest; single participants are not allowed.
  • Any disclosure of problem discussions or solutions outside of the team prior to the end of the contest is prohibited.
  • For other rules, see here.
